title: Robust audit pipeline contracts and failover strategies for 3rd-party sinks
creator: Priya Khatri
description: Define a resilient, observable, and versioned delivery contract for audit events sent to external sinks (SIEMs, Splunk, Datadog, and customer webhooks). Implement deterministic idempotency, DLQ/backoff semantics, and a cost-effective fallback for extended outages so customer audit pipelines remain intact and debuggable.
background: Current audit delivery is best-effort HTTP/webhook with occasional retries; teams have observed duplicate events, long tails during partial outages, and limited visibility into why an event landed in a DLQ. Enterprise customers require clear delivery semantics, per-tenant encryption, and a documented failover path to comply with audits and incident postmortems.
proposed_solution: 1) Define an audit envelope schema v2 with fields: event_id (uuid), tenant_id, seq_no (optional monotonic per-tenant), version, timestamp, payload_type, signature (HMAC), and transforms metadata. 2) Delivery semantics: at-least-once delivery with required idempotency_key derived from event_id; sinks must support idempotency or server will dedupe within retention window. 3) Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts configurable per sink (default 5 attempts over 24h). 4) DLQ behavior: after max attempts, route event to tenant-scoped DLQ (encrypted in object storage) and emit an alert. 5) Short-term buffer: local persistent ring buffer per-shard + append-only object store (S3/GCS) for durable spillover during infra failures. 6) Fallback export: scheduled bulk export from DLQ to customer-configured S3 path or support team-managed Splunk HTTP bulk ingest. 7) Observability: metrics, per-event trace IDs, request/response snapshots (sanitized) and an audit delivery dashboard with audit.log.delivery_success_rate, p95 latency, and DLQ counts. 8) Security: per-tenant envelope encryption using customer KMS for Private deployments, HMAC signing for hosted integrations, rotation policy for signing keys.
tradeoffs:
- At-least-once simplifies delivery guarantees but requires dedup logic at consumers or server-side dedupe window which increases memory/metadata overhead.
- Adding durable spillover (S3) increases storage cost but significantly improves durability for long outages.
- Per-tenant KMS adds key management complexity and latency when encrypting small events; for hosted customers we default to HMAC+KMS-protected signing keys to balance cost and security.
- Strict sequence enforcement would provide stronger ordering but would increase head-of-line blocking and reduce throughput for high QPS tenants.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Implement envelope v2 schema and server-side idempotency window + basic retry policy; dogfood internally with platform-internal tenants. Phase 2: Enable per-tenant DLQ + S3 spillover for a small set of enterprise customers with dedicated onboarding. Phase 3: Expose full sink configuration UI in Console and opt-in automatic fallback exports. Phase 4: Default-enable for all Dedicated/Private tenants after one month of monitoring.
Each phase includes migration tooling to re-sign or rewrap legacy events if required.
monitoring: metric:audit.delivery.latency_p95 - goal < 10s for webhooks under normal conditions
metric:audit.dlq.count - alert if > 0.1% of daily events or any tenant > 50 events/day
metric:audit.buffer.spilled_bytes - alert on sustained growth over 1h
log:trace.audit_event_id - allow linking request traces to delivery attempts
alert:audit.delivery.error_rate - fire if error rate > 5% over 30m for >= 3 tenants
testing_plan: unit: schema validation and HMAC verification tests
integration: end-to-end delivery to Splunk HEC, Datadog logs intake, and customer webhooks with synthetic tenants
chaos: kill delivery workers and verify ring buffer + S3 spillover recovers without loss
load: 10k events/sec synthetic per-region to validate backpressure and batching behavior
security: key rotation and signature validation test matrix for hosted vs private deployments
acceptance_criteria: defined envelope v2 contract published in Confluence
server implements idempotency dedupe window and honors idempotency_key
retry policy is configurable per-sink and defaults applied
DLQ + S3 spillover exists and a tenant's DLQ can be exported successfully within UI/CLI
platform metrics show delivery_success_rate >= 99.9% for dogfood tenants over 7d
integration smoke tests pass for Splunk, Datadog, and generic HTTP webhook
security review completed and key rotation docs published
